raw_response:
*Thinking as this farmer, in her own voice:*

---

The wheat is already in the ground — I put it in last October, same as I've done for thirty years. Eight mu in the north and middle plots. I used my own saved seed again this year, from the cleanest-looking grain I set aside at harvest. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — one bag of the blue 50-jin bags for every three or four mu. Not exact, just how I've always done it. My neighbor Sister Chen does the same, she gets good wheat.

Now it's spring. The wheat looks decent — a bit pale in one corner where the soil is thinner. At jointing I'll add some urea, about half a bag for every three mu or so. I'll irrigate three times for wheat this year: once now before jointing if it stays dry, once at heading, and once when the grain is filling. The well we share with three other households — I have to schedule it, I can't just pump whenever I want.

Harvest is early June. I hire the combine. Eighty yuan a mu is a lot, but I can't cut 8 mu by hand fast enough, and if you're slow you lose grain to the rain.

Right after wheat comes off — and I mean that same week — I need the maize in. My husband comes back from town for this stretch. We get someone with a rotary tiller to work the wheat stubble down, then we plant, mostly by hand with a dibble tool though I'm thinking about hiring the planter this year since my back has been bad. Hybrid seed, I buy fresh every year, those small bags from the seed shop. One bag covers about three mu. I put compound down at planting — less than for wheat, maybe one bag for four mu — and then I topdress with urea when the plants are chest-high. Whether I irrigate depends on whether it rains in July and August. Last year I pumped twice because it was dry. A normal year maybe once or not at all. Irrigation costs money — the electricity meter runs.

My stevia is in the south plot, 4.4 mu. This is where I make real cash income. The company sends a truck to collect — I don't have to take it anywhere or negotiate a price, which suits me fine. Stevia is perennial but I replace dead plants each spring with seedlings, maybe half a mu worth. First cut is June, second in August, third in late September or early October before frost. The June cut overlaps with wheat harvest and maize planting, which is very hard. I hire three or four women from the village for two or three days. August and October I can manage with my daughter-in-law and whoever else is around.

For stevia fertilizer I keep it simple: some compound in spring when growth starts, then a bit of urea after the first cut and again after the second. It doesn't need as much as wheat. I water it twice in the hot months if rain is short.

My biggest worry this year is the June crunch. Wheat harvest, maize planting, AND first stevia cut — all within two or three weeks. I'm already thinking about who I can ask to help and keeping some cash back from selling the wheat. Last year I almost missed the right planting window for maize because I couldn't get the rotary tiller on time.
